Extra read-only folders you may use: handoff-docs, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fqq-Desktop-Topflightapps-roundai/2a408671-6ff1-4104-9d24-9f97da7d0ee6/scratchpad/cr/review-evidence

Scenario TC-14/S21 — The full retry sequence stays within about 30 s

Requirements it checks:
- T9: The full retry sequence stays within about 30 s.
- U15: Generate timing: each run logs how long the AI call itself took, separately from the total; any run over 30 s where the AI service was not the cause is reviewed with Vikram. Timings are targets, not Pass/Fail.

Given: convex/ai/providers/retry.ts on main: CALL_BUDGET_MS 30000, ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS 20000, MIN_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS 8000, RETRY_DELAY_MS 1000, RETRY_PRIMARY_IF_FAILED_WITHIN_MS 10000; unit tests e2e/unit/provider-retry.unit.ts (RT-07, RT-08)
When: Review the budget code and the unit test results for slow Haiku, slow retry, and a fallback that starts late
Then: Haiku, its retry and the Mistral fallback together finish or fail within about 30 s, and the fallback always gets at least 8 s. Computed worst case on main: a temporary Haiku failure at just under 10 s, the 1 s pause, a second Haiku try capped at the remaining 19 s, then the 8 s Mistral floor: about 38 s. A temporary failure that took 10 s or more skips the Haiku retry (RT-07)
Oracle: Doc review against TFA-94422 AC 7, judged on the computed worst case (about 38 s), not on RT-08 alone: RT-08 checks that each deadline comes from the remaining budget but does not model the slow-first-failure path. Whether about 38 s is 'about 30 s', and whether skipping the retry after a slow temporary failure meets AC 2, is Q22. Self-review item D (a long Mistral note can hit the 20 s per-attempt cap) is recorded for a human. On the local stack this cannot be forced without aiProvider:_set or a fault hook, both out of bounds

THE ORACLE WINS. The question below only scopes this scenario to what code can decide. If the question, or its pass/fail rule, ever reads differently from the Then/Oracle above, follow the Then/Oracle, give the verdict the oracle gives, and say where they differ in openQuestions.

Open questions the oracle defers to, with the oracle's default for each (do not settle them yourself):
- pending:Q22 — oracle: "Whether about 38 s is 'about 30 s', and whether skipping the retry after a slow temporary failure meets AC 2, is Q22". Default: a computed worst case of about 38 s, or a skipped retry after a slow temporary failure, is labelled pending:Q22

Gaps the matrix already records (use the id in a label only when the finding is exactly that gap):
- (none)

YOUR QUESTION (answer this, from the code):
From convex/ai/providers/retry.ts (and the callers that run Haiku then Mistral), compute the worst-case wall time of a Haiku attempt, its retry and the Mistral fallback, with every constant cited (CALL_BUDGET_MS, ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS, MIN_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS, RETRY_DELAY_MS, RETRY_PRIMARY_IF_FAILED_WITHIN_MS or whatever the file really has). Show the worst path step by step. The unit tests RT-07/RT-08 were run in the static lane (staticEvidence repo-checks.json, unitTests): context only.

pass = the whole sequence finishes or fails within about 30 s and the fallback always gets at least 8 s
fail = the computed worst case is above about 30 s (show the path), or the fallback can get less than 8 s. A worst case of about 38 s is the case the oracle hands to Q22: label it pending:Q22; a worst case well beyond that, or a fallback under 8 s, is a plain fail (label new)

Other halves of this scenario that another lane or a person runs (do not judge them; if the code you read predicts one of them, report that as a finding labelled half:<name>, supports = pass or fail):
- (none)

Not part of this verdict (other scenarios, or notes that decide nothing here):
- real slow-provider timing cannot be forced on the local stack (oracle)
- self-review item D (a long Mistral note can hit the 20 s per-attempt cap) is recorded for a human

Static-lane files you may read for context (scripted, same commit; never cite them as evidence): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fqq-Desktop-Topflightapps-roundai/2a408671-6ff1-4104-9d24-9f97da7d0ee6/scratchpad/cr/review-evidence/repo-checks.json

Label every finding:
- new: a failing point the matrix does not already record (supports = fail)
- known:<id>: exactly one of the recorded gaps listed above
- pending:<id>: a failing point whose verdict the oracle hands to one of the open questions above
- half:<name>: a point about one of the other halves above
- context: background, not for or against the verdict
